    WORTH IT. SEARCH NO MORE. CARPLAY IN MAZDA

    Reviewed in the United States on January 19, 2019
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I installed it in my 2016 MX5. I now have CARPLAY!. Much better than the mazda infotainment system. Having read all the question I believe is worth to explain what is these part. Carplay needs three things to work, first a iphone ( obviously) , second a viable method that the phone can use to interact with the car unit ( cable, bluetooth) and third a car radio unit that has the protocol to aloud the iphone to take control of the screen. These part resolves the second thing, a viable method to interact with the unit. Why? Older mazda models ( 2014-2018) have usb ports that does not have the power requirements or the speed to be able to make CARPLAY magic happen, that is why you need these part, a replacement for youre USB HUB. But buying it alone will not cut it. You need the third thing a car radio unit with the software to been able to interact with youre phone. These was accomplished by mazda with the 7.x an above software version. You need, if you buy these part to take , in these order, these steps in order to make it work. First you have to update the software to the 7.x version. Either by going to a dealership or by doing it youre self. Where can you get the software if not in a dealer. Thera are mazda forum that offer them free. I used the Mazda3revolution forum. Be ware you have to follow instructions there to update the software. The softwares are world regions specific. Find yours. Only when you have accomplished that, you can install these part. Install is easy, i recommend using trim tools ( very cheap bought mine in amazon). The interaction with carplay is nice. It lets you use all hese features: use waze, googlemaps, spotify, applemusic direct on youre screen. The audio is separated from carplay it self. What does these mean? You can listen to a radio station and have the carplay screen on, use googlemaps or waze. Even the navigaton instructions of these app are separated from music audio ( you will hear it on the drivers side as if someone was talking you from youre right) and the music will be keep in low volume in the background. Of course if you choose to listen to spotify, that is what you will hear in the background. Iam very happy, i have know a better driving experience. Last advantage: since the usb port has more power, you phone will be charge quickly ( i would see half charge in 15 to 20 minutes). Very happy

    Reviewed in the United States on March 10, 2020

    Installed in a 2015 Mazda 3 Grand Touring. Followed the excellent installation instructions found online. Also a YouTube video that shows how the plastic bits come apart on the dash and center console.

    Everything came together without a hitch and CarPlay worked the very first time. Total install time about 2 hours including the firmware update that took about 45 minutes.

    Worth $165? I guess so. Having Waze and GoogleMaps on the dash screen makes it worthwhile for me.

    Does what it's supposed to do

    Reviewed in the United States on September 27, 2021
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    We're an Android family, so am using the Android Auto. I got this mainly to get the improved navigation in our CX-9 over Mazda's crappy system. Also to get some better music apps.

    Installation was pretty easy, especially if you use fish tape to go through the center console to retrieve the wiring. Try a coat hanger if you don't have fish tape. There is no need to disassemble the whole center console.

    Just don't make the same mistake I did after you're finished. I turned everything on and grabbed a USB cable I had in a drawer to connect my phone, and nothing worked. After thinking for a while that I must have done something wrong, I scrounged around for a different USB cable, and it worked. Turns out I had first grabbed a charging cable, so the data wires were not connected.

    Also, make sure you are at the correct firmware version for the head unit before you begin, otherwise it won't work. Make sure you watch Youtube videos to see what you're in for before purchasing, and make sure you can still get the firmware. It used to be readily available, but Mazda has been blocking some sources for it, so you may have to go to dealership for the firmware update. I had updated my firmware months ago while updates were still readily available online.

    The downside of both the Car Play and Android Auto is that the navigation does not show up on the Head Up Display like the OEM navigation does. Also, this is not a wireless connection, so you need to plug your phone into the USB every time you get in the car.

    If you use navigation a lot, this is worthwhile. Can't really comment on the call/text interface, because I don't talk or text when driving.

    If nothing else, it's a fun DIY project for us techno-nerds.

    Installation looks more intimidating than it actually is...

    Reviewed in the United States on February 16, 2020
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    I do this kind of work on a daily basis. To be truthful, even I was a little reluctant to tear my dash apart before making my first car payment. However, I felt way more comfortable doing this work on my own vehicle than having else do it.

    First, watch the YouTube videos several times to get acclimated. Make sure you have the most recent firmware installed (mine was up to date). Use a plastic trim removal tool for panel disassembly. Have electronic wipes, and micro-fiber towels on hand to keep the work environment clear of fingerprints and smudges. Keep your work area clean and well lit. The installation took less than 1 hour (since I didn't have to deal with software updates).

    Been using CarPlay for navigation and phone calls. There is a little bit of a leaning curve but I really think its value exceeds the investment.

  • rael gabriel
    5 out of 5 stars
    Verified Purchase

    For the experienced DIYer

    Reviewed in the United States on January 1, 2020
    Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
    Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

    First of all, everyone that says they did it in 30 minutes is a liar, or using internet time (multiply by 4 for real world time). It takes a good hour to upgrade the firmware alone, if you include searching for the file and getting a thumb drive written. When you do the actual firmware upgrade, it takes the car 30 minutes itself (while you collect the tools for the hardware install).

    As others said, a trim tool(s) is necessary to remove several of the interior trim pieces. A 10mm socket with extension is used for one bolt. Phillips screwdriver and wire cutter (to cut ends of cable ties) complete the toolkit.

    The most thorough thread has been removed from the Mazda3 forum, but youtube videos are helpful. On my daughter's 2018 Mazda3 HB, I had to loosen center console enough to pull it back a few inches. This freed up front panel to get behind the old hub to push it out the front. I used a long flathead screwdriver to break the top notches from behind, which helped removal.

    Product works great, if you have used Carplay before you know what to expect. No more vent phone holders or balancing phone on the steering wheel!

    My install time:

    researching firmware update - 30 minutes

    burning flash drive - 15 minutes

    installing update firmware in car - 45 minutes

    disassembling interior and removing hub - 1 hour

    hooking up new hub and trying out - 15 minutes

    tidy-up wiring, reassemble interior - 15 minutes

    Total time of 3 hours

    I work on my cars a lot, last big job was installing coilover suspension, this is MUCH easier. Just don't think you'll get it done in 30 minutes! Note some Mazda models might be easier (or harder) than mine.
